<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ca80f05ec5c6aab22f31553cb5f8737a17450563` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2c2fd40673cc2c709e008a09b4adaf84d9b4689e` — the merge of head `433f7f2005c1d37a3eb8fea3569d9b874103aee4` into base `ca80f05ec5c6aab22f31553cb5f8737a17450563`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2c2fd40673cc2c709e008a09b4adaf84d9b4689e && git checkout 2c2fd40673cc2c709e008a09b4adaf84d9b4689e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ca80f05ec5c6aab22f31553cb5f8737a17450563 433f7f2005c1d37a3eb8fea3569d9b874103aee4 && git checkout -B drift-repro ca80f05ec5c6aab22f31553cb5f8737a17450563 && git merge --no-ff 433f7f2005c1d37a3eb8fea3569d9b874103aee4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ca80f05ec5c6aab22f31553cb5f8737a17450563
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ca80f05ec5c6aab22f31553cb5f8737a17450563` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #25610 · `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01PC4NPXPgPmpDRG9DdDnyXT` · 2026-10-24T12:58Z · head `433f7f2005` · report `6384295899` · seat review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Both clause-② limbs hit (path: `packages/spec/src/automation/io-node-config.zod.ts`; declaration: `Clause-②: yes`), so a same-shape `## Contract review` PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the landing head is owed. `needs:contract-review` is added in this stroke. That tier is still behind its quota wall (HTTP 429, re-probed at this record), so this PR stays draft until the review runs.

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #25610`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added` and `Ruling-ref: 6377731715` are line-initial. The changeset is `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/lint` and carries both declarations. 17 files, +682/−22 (`get_files`), all inside the claim's surface: the spec schema and its two test files, the lint member, its suite wiring and test, generated files (`api-surface`, `authorable-surface`, `declaration-map`, `export-origins`, `json-schema.manifest`, the strictness-ledger counts, two reference pages), and the changeset. Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 25645`: 704 lines). No `content/docs/releases/`.
2. **The ruling, measured on the diff.** Letter B for #25444, under 6377842908's execution condition: 「收件人只能来自记录的 email 类型字段，⛔ 不接受自由文本或表达式拼出的地址」.
   - `NotifyEmailFieldRecipientSchema` is a closed `{ emailField }` arm whose value must match the `FieldSchema.name` grammar. It is the fourth arm of `NotifyRecipientsSlotSchema`, after the CEL envelope, so a string still parses as a recipient string and an envelope as an envelope. Neither an address nor an expression can parse as this arm.
   - `@objectstack/lint`'s reference-integrity member `validateNotifyEmailFieldRecipients` resolves the field against the trigger object (the start node's `objectName`, or `timeRelative.object`). It refuses an unknown field, a field that is not `email`-typed, and a flow with no typed triggering record.
   - The rate limit and messaging log are #25571's, as the claim set.
3. **Changeset, checked line by line against the diff.**
   - "a string in `recipients` stays a user id or an audience selector, and an envelope stays a CEL value": the union order and the arm's closed shape.
   - "The node names `email` as its only channel … a node with no `channels`, or one naming any other channel, is refused": the new `superRefine` arm on `NotifyConfigSchema` at `channels`.
   - "The form is the whole `recipients` value, never a list entry": the list branch of `notifyRecipientsRefusal`.
   - The three lint rule ids match the member.
   - "until it does, a run that reaches such a node fails at the node": on `origin/main`, `service-automation` `notify-node.ts` `resolveRecipients` (about `:207`–`:240`) returns `ok: false` for any evaluated non-string item ("…, not a recipient"). Read, not executed.
4. **Gates.** Check-runs on `433f7f2005` at this record: 41 in all; 31 success, 6 skipped (opt-in and path-filtered), 4 in progress (Test Core 2/6–5/6), 0 failed. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are both `success`. Local, per the report:
   - 113/113 derived, all exit 0, `--ran` DERIVED zero.
   - spec 715 files / 21704 tests; lint 159 files / 7243 tests; consumer `service-automation` typecheck and 199 files / 2628 tests.
   - Ablations: the lint type check 3 red, the spec channel check 4 red, both restored.
   - Landing waits for every check green and the contract-review PASS.
5. **Deviations accepted.**
   - (a) The claim's liveness-ledger row is disproved: `FlowNodeSchema.config` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` and `flow.json` holds `nodes.config` as a childless leaf. This matches the measurement on PR #25632. The `[not live yet]` sentence in the `recipients` describe and the changeset are the record; #25571 removes it when delivery lands.
   - (b) One `origin/main` merge (`8040d181`, bringing #25617), with only the touched files re-tested after it, declared.
   - (c) One gate finding (`check:spec-parsed-alias`, ADR-0122) fixed in `2a26b7e90b`.
   - `mcp_calls` 0; relay writes 2.
6. **Open questions and out-of-scope outcomes.**
   - Whole-value only, and `email` as the only channel: both decided by the dev, beyond the ruling's words. Accepted as narrow on purpose: widening either later is non-breaking, and narrowing after release is not. The contract review answers them as boundary flags.
   - `notify-email-field-no-trigger-record` also refuses an action-launched flow that can bind a record. The ruling says "the triggering record", and no static binding exists for that case. Boundary flag for the contract review.
   - The existing path that mails a written-out or computed address (`email-channel.ts` `EMAIL_SHAPE`; the resolver keeps an unmatched email verbatim). Whether the ruling's second clause reaches it is the maintainer's call, and a narrowing would break 5 showcase nodes. Carried by the decision card #25647.
   - `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`, and removing the describe's not-live sentence: carried by #25571 (the dev's finding; the seat posts a pointer there at merge).
7. **Landing.** Not governed, 704 changed lines. Once a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS is on record and every check on the then-current head is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay.
